notes__: Azerbaijan introduced Targeted Social Assistance (TSA) on July 1, 2006. It is a means tested program run by the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of Population. It is completely financed by the state budget and meant to help certain groups to avoid falling into poverty. The level of social assistance given in Azerbaijan is defined by the level of need. This was set at €42.56 (60 AZN) per capita in 2008 and €57.4 (65 AZN) for 2010. The number of people receiving such aid has increased every year. In 2007, only 48,705 families (218,673 people) or 2.5% of the population received this aid and by the end of 2009, 163,409 families (749,965 people) or 8.4% of the population were eligible to receive it (The State Statistical Committee of the Republic of Azerbaijan, 2009b). The average amount of assistance for one family in the country is €86.81 (98.19 AZN) and it is €19.06 (22 AZN) for one person. ***Spending from 2009 on was corrected based on data obtained from TTL (Feb 2013)

Семейный капитал (зачисление на депозитные счета граждан)
benefity_type_expl: Families giving birth to the third and subsequent children are rewarded with a cashless lump-sum deposit in the amount of $10,000. Eligible for the bonus are Belarusian citizens who give birth to or adopt the third and subsequent children in the period of 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2019. Families will be able to use the money when a child turns 18. The money can be used to improve housing conditions, get education or other services, including social services and healthcare services, or be deposited to a mother's pension account. The money can be used before a child turns 18 only if a family needs to pay for the medical services included in the list of the Ministry of Healthcare. The financing is provided in U.S. dollars.
spending_source: added by U. Valetka April 2016, GASP spending data from MLSP, Department of Family Policy
notes__: data for January-September 2015

sub_category: Family and child allowance (including orphan and vulnerable children benefits)
benefity_type_expl: BJA provides cash after verifying the pregnant mother of children below 2 years got a health services promoted by the program
conditionality_type: (i) Attend prenatal controls at the assigned health centre, according to a timetable delivered at the time of registration; (ii) Have an institutional delivery (performed in a health center); (iii) Attend postnatal health controls till children is 24 months (6 controls per year, totalizing 12 controls).
frequency_payment_other: (i) The mother receives Bs.50 after each of the 4 prenatal controls; (ii) The mother receives Bs. 120 after institutional delivery, and (iii) The mother receives Bs. 125 after each of the 12 postnatal health controls. Resources are receive approx. 60 days after the service.
source_financing: General Treasury of Bolivia, World Bank, IDB
spending_source: UDAPE

notes: Project implemented in two phases, Family Planning included in both phases

contact: Vera Minnik, Project Director, EPOS Health Management, vera.minnik@epos.de, Ph: +855 (0) 12 959 339

sub_category: Targeted subsidies: Health benefits and reduced medical fees for vulnerable groups
notes: Upon the discussion with the consultant Karl hoyning decided to keep udner other exemptions. The scheme  works indirectly. Hospitals are reimbursed for fees they have forgone when treating a patient that was unable to pay. The subsidy therefore goes to hospitals, not individuals.
targ_other: It is unclear what criteria are used for identifying eligble persons, beyond apparent inability to pay. The programme serves a similar function as the HEFs and similar criteria are - at least in theory - used.
spending_source: Excel sheets in the "Health User Fee Exemptions" folder - 2012 and 2013, National Hospitals and Regional operators in separate documents (each point was made summing the two)
contact: Dr Sok Kanha, Deputy Director of Planning and Health Information, Ministry of Health, kanha@online.com.kh, phone: +855 1262 2107
notes__: 1) Beneficiary numbers are claims, not necessarily unique individuals 2) Administrative cost not available as the scheme is run through the Ministry and staff/operation covered over Ministry recurrent budgets 3) I can only explain the 2012-2013 increase in utilisation vs. The reduced expenditure by reductions of Inpatients at national hospitals, potentially more expensive than regional equivalents.

sub_category: Public works, workfare and direct job creation
program_name: Support to the stabilisation and early recovery of communities at risk in CAR (SIRIRI) Phase 2
program_name_l: Support to the stabilisation and early recovery of communities at risk in CAR (SIRIRI) Phase 2
notes: The proposed project will contribute to stability and reconciliation, conditions essential for durable solutions, through facilitation of joint work opportunities of different ethnic, religious and other community members. It will also improve the economic situation of the population indirectly through the rehabilitation of infrastructure and directly through the cash injected into the local economy through cash for work activities.  These work rotations paired with training opportunities offer an alternative to violence to youth at risk of recruitment by armed groups as well as offering important livelihood opportunities to female headed households and survivors of sexual violence who are most at risk of engaging in survival sex having lost a breadwinner or their own income generation activity due to the conflict.
notes_: European Commission
beneficiary_comments: Bénéficiaires à Désagréger par année. les bénéficiares sont constitués d'hommes et de femmes

sub_category: Food for work (including food for training, food for assets etc.)
program_name: Food-for-Work Program of Poverty Alleviation Fund
benefity_type_expl: Most assessments indicate that the selection of individual participants for FFW was done in an equitable manner. Generally, each household was assigned a certain number of days of FFW work. Richer households sometimes chose not to participate and contribute cash instead. Coupons could be exchanged for grains, cash.
conditionality_type: labor contribution for food aid
source_financing:
Funding for the budgetary grants and, since 1997, also for the FFW program came from the central government budget. Funds provided by the central government required matching by provincial and county governments. 
the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) funds Food-for-Work infrastructure projects, especially for roads and drinking water
implementing_agency: Local government;  different agencies became responsible for different poverty reductions projects and activities (rural roads constructed under the FFW program, for example, have been implemented by local staff of the Transport Bureau)
spending_source:
ILO, Social Security Department
From poor areas to poor people: China’s evolving poverty reduction agenda. An assessment of poverty and inequality in China, World Bank

sub_category: Food for work (including food for training, food for assets etc.)
program_name: Food-for-Work Program of Poverty Alleviation Fund
benefity_type_expl: Most assessments indicate that the selection of individual participants for FFW was done in an equitable manner. Generally, each household was assigned a certain number of days of FFW work. Richer households sometimes chose not to participate and contribute cash instead. Coupons could be exchanged for grains, cash.
conditionality_type: labor contribution for food aid
source_financing:
Funding for the budgetary grants and, since 1997, also for the FFW program came from the central government budget. Funds provided by the central government required matching by provincial and county governments. 
the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) funds Food-for-Work infrastructure projects, especially for roads and drinking water
implementing_agency: Local government;  different agencies became responsible for different poverty reductions projects and activities (rural roads constructed under the FFW program, for example, have been implemented by local staff of the Transport Bureau)

program_name_l: UNICEF - Projet d'Appui a la Mise en Oeuvre des Mesures de Protection Sociales pour la Scolarisation des Eleves Vulnerables
notes: The project is implemented in 1,586 schools in 8 different catholic school districts in the western part of the DRC. The project provides tuition fees waiver for 30 vulnerable pupils by paying 1,150 USD to each school for the academic year. The projected started in August 2015 and will end in June 2016; but negotiations are ongoing to extend it to 2019. It ensures training for teachers, promoting extracurricular activities and tutoring. targ_other: Para ser seleccionado dentro del programa, al inicio de cada curso lectivo cada docente con ayuda del Comité de Nutrición y el Departamento de Orientación, levanta un listado actualizado con la selección de beneficiarios del comedor, basándose en los estudiantes de familias con ingreso económico bajo, problemas nutricionales y discapacitados y/o con sospecha de riesgo psicosocial. La distribución de los recursos entre los centros educativos se realiza mediante una categorización: A, instituciones con bajos índices de desarrollo distrital, B, resto de centros educativos.
source_financing: Fondo de Desarrollo Social y Asignaciones Familiares (FODESAF)
spending_source: Ministerio de Educación Pública (MEP)

sub_category: Family and child allowance (including orphan and vulnerable children benefits)
notes:
The system of State Social Support (regulated by the Act No. 117/1995 Coll., on the State Social
Support, as amended) guarantees direct assistance especially for families with dependent children
in specific social situations when this family cannot resolve these situations with their own forces
and financial means.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs of the CR
notes_:
A parent who personally and duly cares for a child who is the youngest in the family is entitled to parental allowance. Parental allowance is provided until the total amount of 220,000 CZK is drawn, maximum up to 4 years of child’s age.

A parent may elect the amount of parental allowance and thus the period of its drawing under the condition that at least one parent in a family is a person participating in sickness insurance. The monthly amount of parental allowance is calculated based on daily assessment base for determination maternity benefit or sickness benefit related to child’s confinement or adoption according to the act on sickness insurance. If 70 % of 30 multiple of daily assessment base is under or equal 7,600 CZK, the amount of parental allowance can get to 7,600 CZK at the most; if 70 % of 30 multiple of daily assessment base is higher than 7,600 CZK, the maximum amount of parental allowance is limited by this figure, but parental allowance totals no more than 11,500 CZK. When the daily assessment base can be determined for both parents, the higher one is used for calculation. Choice of the amount of parental allowance can be changed once in 3 month.
spending_source: Czech Statistical Office

implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs of the CR
notes_:
A parent who personally and duly cares for a child who is the youngest in the family is entitled to parental allowance. Parental allowance is provided until the total amount of 220,000 CZK is drawn, maximum up to 4 years of child’s age.

A parent may elect the amount of parental allowance and thus the period of its drawing under the condition that at least one parent in a family is a person participating in sickness insurance. The monthly amount of parental allowance is calculated based on daily assessment base for determination maternity benefit or sickness benefit related to child’s confinement or adoption according to the act on sickness insurance. If 70 % of 30 multiple of daily assessment base is under or equal 7,600 CZK, the amount of parental allowance can get to 7,600 CZK at the most; if 70 % of 30 multiple of daily assessment base is higher than 7,600 CZK, the maximum amount of parental allowance is limited by this figure, but parental allowance totals no more than 11,500 CZK. When the daily assessment base can be determined for both parents, the higher one is used for calculation. Choice of the amount of parental allowance can be changed once in 3 month.

conditionality_type: Considered UCT! The LEAP Operational Manual from 2012 only lists the following co-responsibilities: (1) school enrolment and attendance (maximum 20% absenteeism) children in the house aged 5-15 and (2) Children under the age of five have to be vaccinated and visit health  facilities for growth monitoring every 5 months. Households in communities which are not covered by education or health facilities or where supply capacities of existing facilities are insufficient are exempted from these conditions. Compliance monitoring should take place every three months and non-compliant households will receive warnings, house visits and in the case of repeated non-compliance, penalties will apply.

Cash transfers for nutrition are expected to be spent by the
households on nutrition, particularly for children. Therefore, if after
the third transfer the children’s health status shows no improvement
due to wilful neglect, the grant is suspended. Reintegration into
the programme after suspension is possible if the children
show improvement in their weight-to-height measurement.
Cash transfers for health are conditional upon children’s
health being regularly checked (once per quarter) at
health centres for children under six years of age.
Cash transfer for education requires 90 per cent
school attendance for children aged 7–14.2
spending_source: UNDP, 2016: SOCIAL ROTECTION IN AFRICA: INVENTORY OF  ON-CONTRIBUTORY PROGRAMMES

health centres for children under six years of age.

school attendance for children aged 7–14.2

program_name: JKN-PBI - recipients of social health Insurance fee waiver
program_name_l: Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional - Penerima Bantuan Iuran -(JKN-PBI)
targ_other: 40% poorest and near-poor as stated in the Unified Database (UDB)
benefity_type_expl: Subsidized public healthcare insurance program, Defined as poor or near-poor as stated in the Unified Database (UDB)
source_financing: Majority by National budget (APBN). Previously, it was funded by reallocated government budget from the fuel price compensation scheme (2001-2005), right now, the JKN-PBI beneficiariesfrom Jamkesmas is subsidized through the National Budget (APBN), while the JKN-PBI beneficiaries from Jamkesda are paid through the local budget (APBD).
implementing_agency: It was managed under the Ministry of Health, but as it transformed and integrated to the JKN, it is now managed under the Social Health Insurance Agency (BPJS).

Three modalities are being tested: in two community councils the CCT is implemented with hard conditionalities (mandatory compliance with loss of benefits for non-compliance); in two others with soft conditionalities (recommended compliance but no loss of benefits for non-compliance) and strong case management  provided by social workers; and in the two remaining community councils hard conditionalities with strong case management. 
1. EducationConditionalities/Co-responsibilities
The education conditionalities/co-responsibilities apply to children between the ages 6 and 17 (in completed ages). The children have to comply with the following:
? Be formally enrolled in any of the Grades 1 to 7 in an eligible primary school; and
? Attend at least 85% of effective school days per monitoring quarter.
2. HealthConditionalities/Co-responsibilities
The health conditionalities/co-responsibilities apply for children below 60 months of age (5 years). The children have to comply with the following:
?  Conduct regular visits to eligible health facilities according to the EPI Immunisation Schedule of the MOH.
? Conduct visits to health facilities monthly for growth monitoring visits, or attend monthly growth monitoring events carried out by village health workers. 
However, the type of health visit is not monitored. Only if the visit ocurred or not.

notes: Antes era un subprograma llamado: Subprograma de Regularización Jurídica de Menores y Adopciones. sub_category: Emergency support in cash (including support to refugees/returning migrants)
program_name_l: Programa del Fondo para Atender a la Población Afectada por Contingencias Climatológicas
notes: Complicated to keep track of SAGARPA Programs in the recent years: Not a 100 percent sure, but… it seems that this program converted into "Programa de Atención a Contingencias Climatológicas" in 2008 or 2009, and in 2011 then it became the program known as "Programa de Prevención y Manejo de Riesgos". In 2014, this program got merged into different programs. Programa de Prevención y Manejo de Riesgos (Garantías y FOINI) got merged into "Programa de Productividad y Competitividad Agroalimentaria" with other 4 programs. "Programa de Prevención y Manejo de Riesgos (CADENA)" got merged with more than 5 programs into "Programa Integral de Desarrollo Rural". Programa de Prevención y Manejo de Riesgos (Apoyos al Ingreso) got merged into Programa de Comercialización y Desarrollo de Mercados; and Programa de Prevención y Manejo de Riesgos (Sanidades) became Programa de Sanidad e Inocuidad Agroalimentaria.
implementing_agency: Secretaría de Agricultura, Ganadería, Desarrollo Rural, Pesca y Alimentación (SAGARPA)
spending_source: Secretaría de la Función Pública, (2003). Reglas de Operación del  Programa del Fondo para Atender a la Población Afectada por Contingencias Climatológicas (FAPRACC) 2003. . Consulta 21 de junio, 2011. http://www.funcionpublica.gob.mx/scagp/dgorcs/reglas/index.htm

program_name_l: Programme Tayssir des transferts monétaires conditionnels
conditionality_type: Programme applies to rural areas (communes) when they belong to program INDH, that own a poverty rate higher than 30% and a school desertion rate higher than 8%. For children registered in schools belonging to the eligible area, of ages 6 to 15.  CHildren cannot be absent more than 4 times per month in primary school, and 6 times per month in high school.
implementing_agency: AMAS-ministry of Education and vocational training MENFP, and administration structures at central and provincial levels
beneficiary_comments: data assigned under year 2009 corresponds to scholar year 2008/2009 and successively
spending_source: Document received from Ministry of Education. File name "Données sur Tayssir_BM_Registre social unique"; number for 2008 - "Note d’orientation stratégique sur le ciblage et la protection sociale" (2011) WB
notes__: The budget under each year corresponds to the budget allocated for the period of time of Sept of the previous year to June of that year (academic year)

beneficiary_comments: The Medium Term Plan of each Vote / Ministry contained in the Medium-term Expenditure Framework sometimes includes absolute numbers of beneficiaries, sometimes relative numbers such as 20% of the target population.  Since the denominator for the relative numbers is usually not known, they are not converted into absolute numbers.  Further, absolute numbers are often not consistent over years.  This applies to all votes/ministries and the MTPs as well as the Accountability Reports.  Reports from 2000/01 to 2012/13 are used to extract numbers.
spending_source: Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure - various years. UNDP, 2016: SOCIAL ROTECTION IN AFRICA: INVENTORY OF  ON-CONTRIBUTORY PROGRAMMES
notes__: Expenditure on benefits:  Figures from 2003 onward provided by the ministry.  Total programme expenditure include costs for grants, emergency assistance (see 1.1.2 below) and Place of Safety/RCCF (see 4.6.1).  Administrative costs are calculated as the difference between total programme expenditure and the sum of grants, emergency support and place of safety expenses.  The negative figures can be explained with the different sources used.  Total programme expenditure is taken from the budget document, hence they are estimates, while the expenditure on benefits are figures provided by the ministry and hence actual data.

targ_other: Proxy-means test/econometric model
conditionality_type: Health: Pregnant women and in postpartum: medical check-ups attendance; Children under 5 years old: growth check-ups attendance, development and immunization check-ups. Education: Children aged 4 to 17 years: 85% attendance to classes during the bimonthly school period, parents should attend the meetings at the school Training: At least one adult household member: participation in training sessions convoked every two months.
implementing_agency: Secretariat of the Social Protection System
notes_:
Provides family support actions to verify compliance with conditionalities and allow the exchange of information with the beneficiaries about their rights and needs.
The programme began in 2006 focusing on the districts with the highest incidence of extreme poverty, but with the aim of have a full coverage in all the country`s localities. The geographical arrangement of the progress of the programme was organized according to the results of the index of extreme poverty incidence (IPE) based on the Living Standards Survey 2003. In December 2008, the coverage of all localities was 95% complete.
The family support component primarily allows the exchange of information on the status of the beneficiary households and on compliance with the conditionalities.
The component of increased social services supply does not have a clear method of execution yet.
spending_source: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social

The geographical arrangement of the progress of the programme was organized according to the results of the index of extreme poverty incidence (IPE) based on the Living Standards Survey 2003. In December 2008, the coverage of all localities was 95% complete.
The family support component primarily allows the exchange of information on the status of the beneficiary households and on compliance with the conditionalities.
The component of increased social services supply does not have a clear method of execution yet.

program_name: Programme of grants for families to buy food
program_name_l: Bono Familiar para la compra de alimentos
notes: A part of Red de Oportunidades
targ_other: geo/proxy-means/community
conditionality_type:
Health: Children under 5 years must have their vaccinations. Adults and teenagers: Must have their health checks updated (vaccines, pregnancy, Pap smear, in the case of women of reproductive age)
Education: Children over 6 years: school attendance.
Training: At least one adult member of the household: participation in training sessions in food production that runs the MIDA and / or volunteer corps.
implementing_agency: National Secretariat for Coordination and Monitoring of Food and Nutrition Plan (SENAPAN)
spending_source: LAC databse

conditionality_type: etre affecté par des calamités
notes_: It is unclear whether the Fonds de Calamité has ever disbursed for its intended purpose. According to MEFP, the fund did not receive any budget allocations from between 2005 and 2012 and it does not exist in its intended purpose, although it now receives budget allocations (500 million FCFA in 2014). The fund appears to be a mechanism the Ministry of Agriculture uses to maintain disposable budget (mostly used for subsidies to the agriculture sector). In 2013 for example, the GoS decided to cancel 1.8 billion FCFA in debts owed by cotton producers to the CNCAS.

conditionality_type: The SSN project includes complementary workshops (“soft conditions”) to reinforce human capital investments, particularly those associated with maternal and child health. The aim of these workshops will be to provide beneficiary households with information on project objectives, encourage beneficiary households to put the transfers toward investments in human capital and to adopt good practices (e.g., on proper health and nutrition, child care, home hygiene, water usage and other topics). The workshops are held on a quarterly basis and beneficiary attendance is encouraged (e.g., by holding these workshops immediately prior to payments), but is not mandatory nor is any penalty applied for not attending.
implementing_agency: NaCSA (Building of systems Social Protection Secretariat)

notes:
Non emergency - Component of the PPRO launched a country strategy (2014–2017).. Food and Nutrition Assistance for Relief and Recovery, Supporting Transition and Enhancing Capabilities to Ensure Sustainable Hunger Solutions PRRO
In South Sudan’s first year of statehood, WFP focused on providing life-saving relief assistance, primarily through general food distributions; in 2012, it launched a country strategy (2014–2017). This protracted relief and recovery operation is part of that strategy, which has four pillars: i) meeting the emergency food needs of vulnerable groups; ii) improving community resilience and livelihoods; iii) expanding market access and the food value chain; and iv) enhancing access to social services in support of good nutrition and learning. WFP’s strategy is guided by the need to increase the capacity of state institutions and enhance partnerships to promote sustainable hunger solutions

notes: Zakat is a religious levy enforced by the government as an obligation under Islam and is mandatory as means of redistributing wealth from the better off to the most needy. Zakat is regulated under the Zakat Act 1986, amended 2001; is a semi-autonmous agency of the Ministry of Welfare and Social Security. It expends cash, in-kind and for emergencies of all sorts. average_benefit: As in 2015, the beneficiary household received each month 120 TND during the first quarter and 150 TND for the rest of the year. .
notes_:
1. Decree n° 457-89 of 29 Mars 1989 related to the delegation of authority from the members of the government to the governors.
2. A joint information circular from the Minister of Interior and the Minister of social Affairs n° 21 of 20 August 1987 related to the National Program of Needy Families.
3. Circular from the Minister of Social Affairs n° 5 of 12 May 1998 delegating the PNAFN’s management to regions and using poverty register.
4. Circular from the Minister of Social Affairs, Solidarity and Tunisian Abroad n° 11 of 28 August 2009 related to PNAFN and poverty register.

program_name: Direct Income Support under the Expanding Social Protection Programme (ESP)
program_name_l: Direct Income Support under the Expanding Social Protection Programme (ESP)
source_financing:
Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda); UK
Department for International Development (DFID); Irish AID; UNICEF
implementing_agency:
Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda); UK
Department for International Development (DFID); Irish AID; UNICEF
notes_: As of March 2016: Baseline for ESP II currently being undertaken. It will establish what proportion of the target population the grant is reaching
beneficiary_comments: Under the new Phase II, beneficiaries will be receiving a 50,000 grant every two months as opposed to 25,000 every month
spending_source: UNDP, 2016: SOCIAL ROTECTION IN AFRICA: INVENTORY OF  ON-CONTRIBUTORY PROGRAMMES
notes__: This program is currently in transtion to phase two of Expanding social protection programme which combined the two components of the Social Assistance Grant for Empowerment (SAGE). The two components are Senior Citzens grant and Vulnerable Families Grant. The program is expected to run from 2015 to 2020 reaching an estimated 128,000 senior citzens (above 65 years) and 17,333 people with disabilities with monthly grant. The program will also scale up to 30 districts from 15 districts

Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda); UK
Department for International Development (DFID); Irish AID; UNICEF
implementing_agency:
Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda); UK
Department for International Development (DFID); Irish AID; UNICEF
notes_: As of March 2016: Baseline for ESP II currently being undertaken. It will establish what proportion of the target population the grant is reaching
beneficiary_comments: Under the new Phase II, beneficiaries will be receiving a 50,000 grant every two months as opposed to 25,000 every month
spending_source: UNDP, 2016: SOCIAL ROTECTION IN AFRICA: INVENTORY OF  ON-CONTRIBUTORY PROGRAMMES
notes__: This program is currently in transtion to phase two of Expanding social protection programme which combined the two components of the Social Assistance Grant for Empowerment (SAGE). The two components are Senior Citzens grant and Vulnerable Families Grant. The program is expected to run from 2015 to 2020 reaching an estimated 128,000 senior citzens (above 65 years) and 17,333 people with disabilities with monthly grant. The program will also scale up to 30 districts from 15 districts

program_name: Restoration of Agricultural Livelihoods in Northern Uganda Component (RALNUC)
program_name_l: Restoration of Agricultural Livelihoods in Northern Uganda Component (RALNUC)
benefity_type_expl: beneficiaries were initially given vouchers however after a monitoring survey indicated that 96% of the farmers had expressed the preference to be paid in cash, a decision was reached to shift to cash therefore beneficiaries received vouchers in one half of the program and cash in the other half.
conditionality_type: membership in a farmers' group that has been selected by the sub-county authorities for participation
implementing_agency: RALNUC Agricultural unit in conjunction with Uganda national agro-input dealers association, ACTED and the Gulu district NGO forum
notes_: RALNUC and DAR have been combined as a component of the current U-Growth programme. The two programmes have a combined budget of $26.5 m for the incoming phase III (2014-2018)
beneficiary_comments: About 56% of the beneficiaries benefited directly from cash or voucher for work projects while the rest benefited in form of farmer's training in agricultural good practices. These numbers are general averages over the 4 year period. All together, between January 2010 and  June 2014, 17,800 earned cash or vouchers worth about $1.1 m while 17,000 benefited from agricultural training.

implementing_agency: RALNUC Agricultural unit in conjunction with Uganda national agro-input dealers association, ACTED and the Gulu district NGO forum

beneficiary_comments: About 56% of the beneficiaries benefited directly from cash or voucher for work projects while the rest benefited in form of farmer's training in agricultural good practices. sub_category: Public works, workfare and direct job creation
program_name: Nothern Uganda Social Action Fund (II) - Public Works Programme
program_name_l: Nothern Uganda Social Action Fund (II) - Public Works Programme
implementing_agency: District Local Government and Office of Prime Minister
beneficiary_comments: The numbers of beneficiaries presented here are total cummulative beneficiaries as opposed to annual beneficaties. Annual beneficiaries figures were not available. We have updated these numbers as follows: Total cumulatve beneficiaries reported in the project completion report are  55,485, who worked for 1,387,433 person days for the whole project life span. in order to get  yearly figures, we divide total person days by total beneficiaries in order to get person days for each individual. (1,387,433/55,485) and arrive at 25 person days per person. we then divide the number of annual person days peovided in the implementation and status report and arrive at estimates of annual beneficiaries.
spending_source: Programme Staff. UNDP, 2016: SOCIAL ROTECTION IN AFRICA: INVENTORY OF  ON-CONTRIBUTORY PROGRAMMES

implementing_agency: Katalemwa Cheshire Home for rehabilation services

beneficiary_comments: Programme staff suggest that the number of beneficiaries reduced because of the withdrawal of three donors who contributed a large proportion of their budget
